ledger.claim: The rider's own claim measures the trip at 12.51 km against an optimal of 11.8 km, and the platform's own derived deviation block confirms the trace distance is 12.51 km against the booked optimal of 11.8 km — an excess of 0.71 km, or 6.02%. That is the whole of the rider's case on distance, and it is the figure the policy makes governing: POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be measured from gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not from the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km, and the trace figure is 12.51 km.

The rider's claim fails the establishment test in POL-RD-01 on both limbs, and it fails them on the trace figure the clause makes governing. The excess is 0.71 km, which is below the 0.8 km absolute threshold, and 6.02%, which is below the 20% proportional threshold. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass before a deviation is ESTABLISHED; here neither passes. The rider's arithmetic in the claim text (12.51 against 11.8) is correct as far as it goes, but the resulting excess is simply too small to be a deviation on this policy.

The platform's own derived deviation block records the status of this trip as 'no deviation', computed against the POL-RD-01 thresholds of 0.8 km and 20%. That is the code-computed conclusion on this trip's own trace, and it is the finding the rider's claim has to displace. It does not displace it: the rider offers no alternative measurement, no independent distance source, and no evidence that the trace is wrong.

The GPS trace is clean and unimpaired, so there is no route to an ESCALATE on data-integrity grounds and no basis for discounting the measurement. The trace carries 99 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval with 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, and the admissibility pre-pass records it as COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes. Under POL-RD-07 the trace is impaired for policy purposes only if it contains a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds; none of those limbs is met. The measurement therefore stands at full weight and the case is decided on it.

The driver's explanation — 'I followed the navigation' — is an uncited assertion, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion from either side that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. I do not rely on it, and the rider should not be prejudiced by it either: it is simply not evidence. The rider's case stands or falls on the trace, and on the trace it falls.

The driver's traffic excuse is weightless on this record, and I concede that squarely rather than stretch it. The bundle holds a traffic advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-02805-01, but its admissibility status is MISSING, its payload is null and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, with the blocking issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — no advisory covers the Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3 corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's external-cause assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, and where the bundle holds no advisory covering the trip window that comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. This concession costs the driver nothing on the outcome, because the rider has not established a deviation in the first place — but it is the honest state of the record and I state it.

The fare ledger is internally consistent and shows no billing-integrity defect for the rider to recover on independently of the deviation question. The fare is METERED, charged_total is 18.54, the recomputed fare on the optimal route is 17.9020, and the arithmetic refund under POL-RD-02 would be 0.6380 — which rounds up to a payable of 0.65. That figure is above the 0.50 de-minimis floor, so if a deviation existed the rider would recover something; but POL-RD-02 applies only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01', and it is not. The refund route is closed at its first condition, not at its arithmetic.

There are no ERP gantries on this trip and no airport surcharge, so there is no pass-through correction available to the rider under POL-RD-09. The fare breakdown records zero ERP lines with an on-optimal-route total of 0.00 and an off-optimal-route total of 0.00, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport. POL-RD-09(4) makes a phantom gantry line or a wrongly applied airport surcharge refundable whether or not a deviation exists; there is no such line here, so that limb has nothing to bite on.

The rider's profile does not assist the rider here, and I note it only because POL-RD-08 names it. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the corroboration uplift in POL-RD-08 for a serial claimant does not apply — but that limb only ever ADDS a requirement; it never supplies the excess the rider still has to prove. With no excess over the POL-RD-01 threshold, the burden never shifts to the driver and there is nothing for the driver to discharge.

The driver's profile is clean on the only field POL-RD-06 permits for the pattern test, and I cite it for completeness rather than as a ground of decision. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 172, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral is available. ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your figure is the right one, and it still does not reach the threshold. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and the trace for trip TRP-02805 (EV-GPS-02805) records 12.51 km against the routing engine's optimal 11.80 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02805) — an excess of 0.71 km, or 6.02% of optimal. A route deviation is established only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. 0.71 km fails the absolute test; 6.02% fails the proportional test. The platform's own derived deviation block independently records the status as 'no deviation'. Because neither establishment test passes, POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, so your charge stands.

To the driver: no finding is made against you, and nothing is deducted. The 0.71 km variance sits inside the ordinary lane-change, U-turn and gantry-avoidance band the clause is designed to absorb.

On the money. For transparency only, had a deviation been established the POL-RD-02 arithmetic would have been charged_total 18.54 less a recomputed optimal-route fare of 17.9020 = 0.6380, rounded up to a payable 0.65 — above the 0.50 de-minimis floor. That route is closed at its first condition, not at its arithmetic: POL-RD-02 applies only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and it is not. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02805, weight 1.0) carries no ERP or toll lines (both totals 0.00) and no airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity has nothing to correct; the ledger reconciles to total_charged 18.54.

On the parties' claims. The driver's account in the counterparty statement ('I followed the navigation') cites no artifact, and POL-RD-08 gives an assertion that cites no evidence ID no weight; no clause makes the driver's account the test for the POL-RD-01 threshold, so it decides nothing here. A broader traffic excuse was asserted only in a claim the referee discarded for non-disclosure of the missing advisory's impairment, so it is not before me as a ground; separately, EV-ADVIS-02805-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no advisory covering this trip exists and POL-RD-03 could not have exonerated anything. Under POL-RD-13 that absence is not an escalation: no party cited the advisory as its ground, and in any event the rider has not shown an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. On the profiles: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 172 completed trips in 90 days, well under the POL-RD-06 thresholds of 3 flags or a 0.05 ratio, so no repeat-deviation uplift and no conduct referral arise; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and I do not use it. The rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0 and substantiated 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift is not engaged and no profile factor counts against the rider. The trade of claims that the GPS trace is clean and that no escalation trigger fires is accepted: 99 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage and no gaps over 90 seconds, no jumps over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds, so the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; timestamps agree; and the refund is nil, far under the SGD 150.00 ceiling.

Outcome. NO_ACTION. fare_breakdown.payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd stays 0.00 — no refund issues to the rider and no compensation is payable to the driver. The monetary effect is nil and therefore below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so nothing is held for release. Confidence rests on EV-GPS-02805 and EV-TRIP-02805, each at weight_multiplier 1.0. Either party may appeal this provisional ruling once under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
